_comment: Category hub pages served by index.php at /<slug>. One entry per category in category-map.php. Titles <= 60 chars, descriptions 150-200, start_here files must belong to the category. Validated by scripts/check_hubs.py (run by scripts/deploy.py --check). Intros are hand-written editorial copy; keep them factual and free of em dashes.

AI & Safety.title: AI Cheat Sheets: Frontier Models, Agents, Safety & Risk
AI & Safety.description: 22 AI cheat sheets: the frontier labs compared, a model picker and API pricing table, coding agents, open-weight models, agentic AI patterns, and the existential-risk case with a p(doom) calculator.
intro: This is the section of the collection I use most at work. The frontier lab comparison, the model picker and the API pricing table are the pages I keep open while building agentic systems, and they get re-verified as the labs ship new models.

The second half is the safety side: a field guide to existential risk, a timeline of the alignment problem, a directory of the safety ecosystem, and an interactive p(doom) calculator that shows which assumptions actually move the estimate. The two halves belong together. You cannot reason about the risk without knowing what the labs are shipping, and you cannot pick a model responsibly without knowing its failure modes.
Start with the frontier labs page if you want the landscape, the model picker if you have a task in hand, and the agentic AI cheat sheet if you are building.

start_here.why: The landscape in one page: eight labs, ranked and compared
Which Anthropic or OpenAI model for the task in front of you
Architecture patterns and failure modes for systems that act

Software & DevOps.title: Software Cheat Sheets: Git, PostgreSQL, .NET, APIs, DevOps
Software & DevOps.description: 25 software cheat sheets for developers and architects: Git commands and internals, PostgreSQL and SQL tuning, .NET and C#, API design, microservices, observability and DevOps pipelines.
intro: These are working references, not tutorials. Each one assumes you already write software and need the command, the default, the tradeoff table or the decision rule without reading a chapter. Git gets two pages: one for the commands you type and one for the object model underneath them, because the second explains every confusing thing the first does.

The architecture pages (.NET clean architecture, API design, microservices, observability, the database comparison) are written for the person who has to choose, so each leads with a comparison table and a rule for when to use which. The language pages (Python and JavaScript for architects, .NET and C#, language design tradeoffs) cover the current versions and date anything that will drift.
If you work on a .NET team, the software development guides hub routes by role. If you just need the command, use the search box; it indexes every section heading on every page.

start_here.why: Commands and workflows, the page most people came for
psql, indexes, EXPLAIN plans, vacuum and replication
Routes by role to the architecture and .NET pages

Security & Privacy.title: Security Cheat Sheets: Linux Hardening, Passkeys, Privacy
Security & Privacy.description: 5 security cheat sheets: a paste-ready Linux server hardening checklist, passkeys and YubiKeys, a personal cybersecurity threat model, post-quantum cryptography and a US data broker opt-out guide.
intro: Five pages, each built to be executed rather than read. The Linux hardening checklist is copy-paste commands in the order you run them on a fresh Ubuntu or Debian box. The passkeys page settles the synced-versus-device-bound question and what to do about recovery. The personal cybersecurity checklist is a threat model first and a tool list second, because most people buy tools for threats they do not have.

The data broker opt-out guide is the tedious one: a step-by-step US procedure for getting your records out of the people-search sites, with the forms and the timelines. Post-quantum cryptography covers the NIST standards and what a migration actually involves; it pairs with the custody-specific version in the crypto custody section.

start_here.why: Run it top to bottom on a new server
Threat model first, then the short list of tools
Passkeys, WebAuthn and recovery without lockout

Risk & Preparedness.title: Preparedness Cheat Sheets: Real Risk, Threat Models, Kits
Risk & Preparedness.description: 10 preparedness cheat sheets: everyday risk in micromorts, what actually endangers kids, how burglars break in, home safe ratings, nuclear fallout survival, gear audits and vehicle emergency kits.
intro: The theme of this section is measuring the risk before buying the gear. The micromort dashboard puts driving, surgery, skydiving and childbirth on one scale. The parent's threat model ranks what actually hurts children (vehicles, water, unsecured firearms, falls) against what parents fear. The security theater audit grades juice jacking, RFID skimming and hotel safes as real, edge case or theater.

Once the ranking is honest, the preparation pages are short: a 72-hour and two-week kit built from the emergencies you will actually face, a vehicle kit for breakdowns and winter, what a home safe rating really buys you, and Kearny's nuclear fallout guidance updated for today. Celestial navigation is here because it is the position-finding method that still works when everything electronic is gone.

start_here.why: Everyday risks on one scale, in micromorts
Rank your real emergencies, then build the kit
Sourced from burglar interviews and BJS data

Bitcoin & Finance.title: Bitcoin & Finance Cheat Sheets: Wallets, Custody, Investing
Bitcoin & Finance.h1: Bitcoin and personal finance cheat sheets
Bitcoin & Finance.description: 9 Bitcoin and finance cheat sheets: hardware wallets compared, a self-custody guide from small holders to whales, exchanges and cards, the whitepaper explained, index investing and US income cliffs.
intro: I run a wallet recovery service, so the custody pages here come from watching how people actually lose coins: bad backups, forgotten passphrases and single points of failure. The wallet comparison and the self-custody guide are written to prevent the cases I see. The whitepaper page walks Satoshi's paper section by section for people who want to understand the system rather than trust it.

The finance half is US-specific and numeric: index investing and tax-advantaged accounts with a FIRE calculator, every income cliff (IRMAA, ACA subsidies, Social Security taxation) on one page, and two calculators that translate income into what a household can actually afford. The monetary standards timeline is the history behind why Bitcoin exists.

start_here.why: Hardware and software wallets compared
Security that scales with how much you hold
Every US income threshold that changes your taxes

Crypto Custody & Compliance.title: Crypto Custody Cheat Sheets: MPC, Compliance, Stablecoins
Crypto Custody & Compliance.h1: Crypto custody and compliance cheat sheets
Crypto Custody & Compliance.description: 10 crypto custody cheat sheets for engineers: MPC wallet architecture, institutional custody tiers, Fireblocks integration, exchange ledger design, KYT and Travel Rule compliance, stablecoin rails.
intro: These pages are for the engineer or architect who has to build or audit digital-asset custody, not for the retail holder (that is the Bitcoin section). They cover the decisions in the order you meet them: which custody model, how threshold signing actually works in production, where the wallet boundary sits in an exchange, and how deposits and withdrawals reach finality on each chain.

The compliance pages place KYT, sanctions screening and the Travel Rule at the correct points in the transaction flow, with an IVMS101 field map. The stablecoin page covers issuer risk, native versus bridged assets and treasury operations. Post-quantum migration and wallet recovery forensics are the two pages nobody wants to need. Start with the custody index; it maps 34 operating decisions against five custody models and says who owns each one.

start_here.why: 34 decisions across five custody models
Threshold signing as deployed, not as in the paper
KYT, Travel Rule and IVMS101 in the right places

Martial Arts & Strategy.title: Martial Arts Cheat Sheets: BJJ, Judo, Karate, Art of War
Martial Arts & Strategy.h1: Martial arts and strategy cheat sheets
Martial Arts & Strategy.description: 5 martial arts cheat sheets: Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu positions and submissions, judo throws and groundwork, Ashihara karate sabaki, a nine-style comparison, and Sun Tzu's Art of War in two languages.
intro: These are the references you want on your phone between classes: the BJJ position and submission map, the judo throw and groundwork catalogue with the Japanese names, and the Ashihara sabaki system. Each is organised the way the art is taught rather than alphabetically, so a technique sits next to the position it starts from.

The nine-style comparison is for the person choosing a school: what each art trains, what it neglects, and how they compare for self-defence, fitness and competition. The Art of War is a dual-language reader, original Chinese beside the English, because the famous quotations are usually paraphrases.

start_here.why: Nine styles compared before you pick a school
Positions, guards, passes and submissions
Throws, groundwork, kuzushi and grips

Firearms & Military.title: Firearms & Military Cheat Sheets: Calibers, Drills, Defense
Firearms & Military.description: 7 firearms and military cheat sheets: handgun calibers and ballistics, modern pistols, rifles and shotguns, concealed carry drills with par times, special forces loadouts and autonomous defense.
intro: The firearms pages are reference tables: caliber ballistics with the history and the arguments, the current pistol, rifle and shotgun landscape, and a set of scored concealed-carry drills with exact courses of fire and par times so practice has a number attached. The loadout page documents what SWAT entry teams, special forces and paramedics actually carry, by role.

The military pages are about where the technology is going: counter-drone systems, collaborative combat aircraft and loitering munitions on one page, the systems-of-systems view of future warfare on another, and a collection of tactical aphorisms with their sources.

start_here.why: 9mm, .45 ACP, .357 and the rest, with the numbers
Scored drills so practice has a standard
C-UAS, CCA and loitering munitions compared

Radio.title: Ham Radio Cheat Sheets: Baofeng UV-5R, Technician, GMRS
Radio.description: 5 ham radio cheat sheets: Baofeng UV-5R programming and a visual quick reference, the FCC Technician study guide for the 2026-2030 pool, a GMRS/FRS/MURS channel chart and an emergency radio card.
intro: The Baofeng pages are among the most-read references on this site, which says something about the manual. The quick reference is the visual one with every button and menu explained; the full guide covers manual programming, CHIRP, repeater offsets, and the legal line between ham, GMRS and FRS use. Read the quick reference first, then the guide when you want to program a repeater.

The Technician study guide is organised by the current 2026-2030 question pool. The channel chart gives GMRS, FRS and MURS frequencies, power limits and repeater pairs on one printable page, and the emergency radio card is meant to be printed and taped inside the radio bag for someone who has never used one.

start_here.why: Every button and menu, explained visually
Manual programming, repeaters, ham vs GMRS rules
Study guide for the 2026-2030 Technician pool

Health & Fitness.title: Health Cheat Sheets: Blood Tests, Sleep, Longevity, Training
Health & Fitness.description: 18 health cheat sheets: blood test results explained, ER or urgent care decision tables, what scary symptoms usually are, longevity biomarkers and supplements graded by evidence, sleep and training.
intro: The medical pages are built from published triage rules and trial data, and they say so on the page. Blood test results explained covers CBC, CMP, lipids, A1c and thyroid without turning every flagged value into a diagnosis. The ER-or-urgent-care page uses real decision rules (Ottawa ankle, PECARN, Canadian CT head). The reassurance tables cover what palpitations, floaters, twitches and lumps usually are, and the specific signs that mean they are not.

The longevity pages rank what the evidence supports, not what sells: the biomarkers that predict lifespan, the interventions that move them, and a supplement ledger that records what each trial actually measured. Number needed to treat puts common drugs and screenings on one honest scale. The training pages (strength, running, cycling, sleep, weight loss) are programming references with zones, volumes and pacing tables.
None of this is medical advice. It is the reference you read before the appointment so the appointment is useful.

start_here.why: Decode the panel without overreading a flag
When to go now, when it can wait
Ranked by evidence, largest effect first

Economics & Politics.title: Economics Cheat Sheets: Systems, Ideologies, State GDP
Economics & Politics.description: 6 economics and politics cheat sheets: a pro-market case for capitalism, economic systems compared, political labels decoded, red vs blue state economies, US states vs countries by GDP, homelessness.
intro: These pages argue a position and show their data. The capitalism page is openly pro-market. The economic systems comparison puts mercantilism, capitalism, socialism and the modern hybrids side by side on ownership, prices and incentives so the differences are structural rather than rhetorical. The political labels page decodes classical liberal, liberal, libertarian, neoliberal, conservative and socialist by what each actually holds.

The data pages are there to replace impressions with numbers: red and blue state economies compared on GDP, income, prices, migration and taxes; US states matched against whole countries by nominal and PPP output; and the homelessness page, which follows rents rather than drugs or poverty and lists the housing rules that push rents up.

start_here.why: Ownership, prices and incentives side by side
What each label actually holds
The numbers, not the narrative

Philosophy & Religion.title: Philosophy Cheat Sheets: Buddhism, Stoicism, Judaism, Islam
Philosophy & Religion.description: 20 philosophy and religion cheat sheets: Buddhism from the Four Noble Truths to anapanasati, Stoicism and its misreadings, Objectivism, Judaism and Shabbat, Islam, and a comparative religion map.
intro: The largest cluster is Buddhist practice, written for a secular reader who wants the method: the core teachings map, the 16 steps of mindfulness of breathing, the four foundations of mindfulness, and a set of debugger pages that treat anger, craving, the five hindrances and speech as systems with known failure modes. Each is grounded in the source texts and says which sutta it is drawing on.

The rest covers traditions and thinkers with the same approach: what the tradition holds, what it practises, what its texts are, and where popular summaries go wrong. Stoicism gets a page on its common misreadings. Objectivism gets a concise statement of its five branches. Judaism, Islam and the Shabbat evening service are reference pages for belief, practice and text, and the comparative religion map lines them all up.

start_here.why: Core teachings and a practice map
Epictetus, Marcus, Seneca, and what gets misquoted
Texts, practices and beliefs compared

Engineering & Science.title: Engineering Cheat Sheets: Rockets, Chips, Metals, Robots
Engineering & Science.description: 25 engineering cheat sheets: orbital rockets compared, Starlink and Tesla specs, humanoid robots, AI accelerators, data center power and cooling, semiconductor manufacturing, nuclear reactors, metals.
intro: The rule for this section is numbers with sources. The rocket comparison lists payload, thrust and reuse for Starship, New Glenn, Falcon Heavy and the rest. The humanoid robot page compares the announced robots by height, payload, battery and actuators. Starlink, Tesla and Boom Overture get spec sheets rather than press coverage.

The data center cluster is the largest: how power gets from the grid to the GPU, when air cooling stops working, the order-of-magnitude numbers everyone in the industry should know, and a page that grades the claims made when a data center is proposed for your town. Semiconductor manufacturing walks wafer to chip. Nuclear reactor types, deaths per terawatt-hour and geoengineering cover energy and climate with the same discipline.
Engineering metals, materials and the sensor comparison are for the person choosing a part. Human evolution and the stellar lifecycle are here because they were fun to build.

start_here.why: Starship, New Glenn, Falcon Heavy by the numbers
The order-of-magnitude numbers for AI data centers
Steel, aluminum, titanium: properties and equivalents

Home & Lifestyle.title: Home Cheat Sheets: Cooking, Electrical, Adhesives, Lawn Care
Home & Lifestyle.description: 18 home cheat sheets: meat temperatures and global cuisines, home electrical basics, bolt torque and tap drill charts, the glue chart, lawn irrigation math, hot tub chemistry and household settings.
intro: Reference pages for the house: the setpoints, ratios and charts you look up once a season and never remember. The household numbers page collects the right settings (water heater, fridge, humidity, tire pressure, filter intervals) instead of the factory defaults. The glue chart is a materials-by-materials matrix. The torque and tap drill chart is the one from the shop wall.

The kitchen pages are meat pull temperatures with carryover, a global cuisine reference by ingredient and technique, and a general cooking guide. Home electrical explains breakers, GFCI and AFCI well enough to know when to call someone. Air and water filtration does the CADR and NSF math so the marketing does not.

A few pages are about how to live rather than how to fix things: how the Amish decide which technology to adopt, what baby gear a baby actually needs, raising multilingual kids, and Caplan's case for having more of them.

start_here.why: Right settings for everything in the house
Pull temperatures with carryover and sous vide
Breakers, GFCI, AFCI and when to call an electrician

Life Admin & Consumer Defense.title: Consumer Defense Cheat Sheets: Scams, Contracts, Claims
Life Admin & Consumer Defense.h1: Life admin and consumer defense cheat sheets
Life Admin & Consumer Defense.description: 15 consumer defense cheat sheets: scam scripts targeting parents and small businesses, debt collector rights, small claims court, contract red flags, flight cancellations and IRS audit odds.
intro: Every page here is a procedure for a situation where the other side does this every day and you do it once. Debt collector calling: the 30-day validation letter and the statute of limitations. Flight cancelled: the parallel rebooking drill and the refund rules. Someone died: the first 72 hours, hour by hour. Suing in small claims: the demand letter, the state limits, and how to actually collect.

The scam pages are scripts and tells: what the calls targeting older parents sound like, the fake invoices and compliance letters that target small businesses, and a family code word protocol. The money pages are about not overpaying: 53 paid services with a free version, why glasses cost $400 and how to pay $40, insurance products stamped buy, skip or trap, and dealer service upsells graded against the owner's manual.

start_here.why: Scripts, tells, and a family code word
The 30-day letter and your rights
Sue, defend, and collect
